nodes.question: Comparing the source and edited images, has the mug been moved to the right of the headphones, rather than merely having a mug appear there?
nodes.criteria: Complete if the edited image shows the requested mug to the right of the headphones and its source position is no longer occupied by that mug, with no clear residual or duplicate indicating the move was not completed. Partial if a mug appears to the right of the headphones but the source position remains occupied by the mug or a clear remnant/duplicate indicates incomplete relocation, or if there is other clear progress toward the requested move without completion. Absent if there is no visible progress toward moving the mug to the right of the headphones. Unknown if the source and edited images do not provide sufficient evidence to assess progress or completion. Do not infer object identity, attributes, or source position beyond what is visually supported.
nodes.binding: The mug and headphones in the source and edited images; compare their visible positions and the source location for evidence of relocation, duplication, or residual artifacts.

program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.
